changes.old: Changes in satellite-mapped water can inform climate-resilient management only when observation support is explicit. We assessed annual seasonal and permanent water source classes in Naogaon, Chapainawabganj and Rajshahi, northwestern Bangladesh, using JRC histories and gridded climate data. The primary 2000–2021 analysis used a retrospectively selected, annually observed footprint of 1,276.41 km². Exploratory reanalysis compared seven footprint/validity cohorts, multi-year windows, simpler climate models, approximate uncertainty estimates and chronological hindcasts. Seasonal source-class area fell from 938.53 to 699.91 km² between the endpoints (25.42%); comparison of the first and final five-year means gave a smaller decline of 14.70%. A footprint based on water observed in 2000–2004 and annual validity through 2021 gave an 18.79% five-year decline. Negative seasonal coefficients persisted across the tested models, although interval and district support varied. Permanent-class gains were sensitive to observation and processing controls. Static river and 2020 cropland context separated contrasting mapped trajectories without identifying their causes. During 2015–2024, raising the Dynamic World threshold from 0.5 to 0.7 increased conditional radar–optical agreement from 89.04% to 98.71%, while mean paired support fell from 11.07% to 3.29%; wet-season support was particularly sparse. Assisted interpretation of 720 sampled pixel-months assigned 76.54% of design-weighted area-time, with 98.56% conditional agreement but no independent accuracy estimate. No actual drought-recovery duration was identified under nine support/reference specifications. Synthetic pulse diagnostics retaining real gaps and envelope widths also failed to confirm the tested deficits. The results identify a restricted-footprint seasonal decline and the observation requirements for investigating it; district-wide water storage, causal abstraction effects and independently validated resilience remain unmeasured.

A two-year joint-cell pilot retained all twelve months of 2018 and 2024, four regions (three districts and their union), three historical-water cohorts and all four confidence thresholds. The eight authenticated quarter exports comprised 288 region/cohort/month rows and used the frozen scene snapshot and radar track. Each product pair was partitioned into both-water, first-water/second-nonwater, first-nonwater/second-water and both-nonwater areas. The first/second products were SAR/Dynamic World and Dynamic World/JRC, respectively. Symmetric positive agreement was twice both-water area divided by twice both-water plus discordant area; negative agreement used twice both-nonwater in the corresponding ratio. Product-specific water prevalence used the same paired denominator. Monthly areas were summed as area-time (km²-month); support denominators retained every intended month, including zero-support months. Empty denominators remained unavailable. These descriptive product comparisons do not estimate sensitivity, specificity or independent physical-water accuracy.

changes.old: Seasonal support and class-specific diagnostics are shown in Figure 8. At thresholds 0.5 and 0.7, mean paired support during June–September was only 0.313% and 0.110% of the union historical-water cohort, versus 16.45% and 4.87% in other months. A bounded November 2024 score-stage probe examined one land-context area and three stable-source-water interiors. Maximum raw water scores were 0.619 and 0.753, respectively, and monthly-median maxima were 0.506 and 0.748; neither probe retained threshold-0.8 support. These selected areas cannot establish a domain-wide probability ceiling or rule out every processing error. The dated assisted comparison also differed between water and nonwater agreement, particularly in Naogaon. Neither diagnostic is an independent accuracy assessment. Full radar model and joint-cell tables retain unsupported combinations.

The completed 2018/2024 pilot reproduced all 35 original area columns to within 10⁻⁶ km² and reconciled every four-cell partition with its paired area. For the union historical ever-water cohort, SAR–Dynamic World pooled agreement increased from 88.92% at threshold 0.5 to 99.45% at 0.7, while paired support fell from 12.91% to 3.34% of intended area-time. At 0.7, Dynamic World classified 99.29% of the paired area-time as water; symmetric water agreement was 99.72%, compared with 72.14% for nonwater (Figure 8D). For Dynamic World–JRC, threshold-0.7 pooled agreement was 98.06%, water agreement 99.01% and nonwater agreement 42.02%, on 3.89% paired support. Only one of four June–September months in each pilot year had any SAR–Dynamic World pair at thresholds 0.5–0.7. Threshold 0.8 supplied no joint cells. All years, cohorts, seasons, thresholds and directional disagreement cells remain in the archived tables; these selected summary numbers do not extend the joint-cell pilot to the full decade.

changes.old: Figure 8. Seasonal and class-specific limits to satellite agreement. (A) Mean SAR–Dynamic World paired support in June–September and other months during 2015–2024, retaining zero-support months. (B) Agreement pooled by paired area-time in those seasons. (C) November 2024 maximum raw and monthly-median probabilities in one small land-context probe and three stable-source-water interiors; probes are selected diagnostics, not independently labeled validation sites. The dashed line is threshold 0.8. (D) Symmetric positive (water) and negative (nonwater) agreement between JRC and assigned assisted labels, pooled across the four sampled months within district; unresolved weight is excluded from these conditional ratios. Assisted labels and optical lineage prevent interpreting them as independent accuracy.
changes.new: Figure 8. Seasonal and class-specific limits to satellite agreement. (A) Mean SAR–Dynamic World paired support in June–September and other months during 2015–2024, retaining zero-support months. (B) Agreement pooled by paired area-time in those seasons. (C) November 2024 maximum raw and monthly-median probabilities in one small land-context probe and three stable-source-water interiors; probes are selected diagnostics, not independently labeled validation sites. The dashed line is threshold 0.8. (D) Symmetric positive (water) and negative (nonwater) product agreement in the completed 2018/2024 union historical ever-water pilot, pooled across all 24 intended months. Product pairs have different support. Threshold 0.8 has no pairs; its class agreement is unavailable. Panels A–B cover ten years, whereas D covers the two pilot years. No panel estimates independent accuracy.

The completed joint cells identify a further selection effect: the high-threshold paired population was almost entirely classified as water. Thus, strong pooled agreement need not imply comparable nonwater agreement. The two-year pilot separated 99.72% water from 72.14% nonwater SAR–Dynamic World agreement, and 99.01% from 42.02% for Dynamic World–JRC. These are symmetric comparisons between products on changing paired populations, not reference-based class accuracies. Their interpretation depends on the retained area, class prevalence and sparse seasonal support. They do not establish the corresponding class-specific ratios in every year of 2015–2024.
